ordered.title: The truth about diesel vs petrol costs
ordered.description: Many owners assume diesel is always cheaper because it's more fuel efficient. Here's why that's not always true.

cards.title: ❌ What many owners think
cards.text: "Diesel is always cheaper because it's more fuel efficient."
cards.fullText: ❌ What many owners think "Diesel is always cheaper because it's more fuel efficient."

cards.title: ✅ Reality
cards.text: Diesel fuel economy is better - but the total cost of ownership is not always lower. Higher repair costs (DPF, EGR, AdBlue), ULEZ/CAZ charges (£12.50/day), higher purchase price, and declining resale value all erode diesel savings.
cards.fullText: ✅ Reality Diesel fuel economy is better - but the total cost of ownership is not always lower. Higher repair costs (DPF, EGR, AdBlue), ULEZ/CAZ charges (£12.50/day), higher purchase price, and declining resale value all erode diesel savings.

blocks.text: "In real UK driving conditions, diesel only makes financial sense for high-mileage, motorway-based drivers. For urban drivers - particularly those in ULEZ/CAZ zones - petrol is often cheaper despite lower fuel economy. The DPF, EGR, and AdBlue costs erode the fuel saving." - Engines Market, [EM-OBSERVED]

Real-world example (15,000 miles/year): Petrol fuel cost £2,045; diesel £1,386 - saving £659. But ULEZ/CAZ charges (if non-compliant) add £3,000+, and DPF/AdBlue issues add £200-£1,500. Net annual cost: petrol £2,045 vs diesel £2,586-£5,886 .

ordered.title: Common questions about diesel vs petrol

blocks.question: Which is cheaper to run - diesel or petrol- +
blocks.answer: It depends on your driving. Diesel has better fuel economy (45-65 mpg vs 30-45 mpg) and lower fuel cost per mile. But diesel engines cost more to maintain (DPF, EGR, AdBlue, timing chain) and face ULEZ/CAZ charges if non-compliant. For high-mileage motorway drivers (15k+ miles/year), diesel is cheaper. For urban drivers with short trips, petrol is cheaper.

blocks.question: Is diesel still worth it with ULEZ charges- +
blocks.answer: Only if your diesel is Euro 6 (2016+) and ULEZ/CAZ compliant. Pre-Euro 6 diesels face £12.50/day ULEZ or £10/day CAZ charges - which can exceed £3,000/year for daily users. If you live in or near a clean air zone and don't have a Euro 6 diesel, petrol is almost always cheaper.

blocks.question: What mileage should I switch from petrol to diesel- +
blocks.answer: The breakeven point is typically 12,000-15,000 miles/year . Below 12,000 miles, petrol is usually cheaper. Above 15,000 miles, diesel starts to make financial sense - especially if you do motorway driving where DPF regenerates properly. Between 12,000 and 15,000 miles, evaluate your specific driving pattern.

blocks.question: Why do diesel engines cost more to replace- +
blocks.answer: Diesel engines have more complex and expensive components: turbocharger, high-pressure injectors, DPF, EGR valve, AdBlue system, and often more labour-intensive timing chains (e.g., BMW N47, Land Rover Ingenium). A reconditioned diesel 4-cylinder costs £700-£1,400 more than the petrol equivalent.

blocks.question: What is DPF and why is it a problem- +
blocks.answer: DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) traps soot particles from diesel exhaust. It regenerates (burns off soot) during long motorway journeys. On short trips, regeneration fails and the DPF blocks - costing £150-£600 to clean or £400-£1,200 to replace. This is why diesel is not recommended for urban drivers.

blocks.question: What is Euro 6 and why does it matter- +
blocks.answer: Euro 6 is the EU emissions standard introduced in 2016. Diesel vehicles must be Euro 6 compliant to enter ULEZ and most CAZ zones without charges. Pre-Euro 6 diesels (2015 and earlier) face daily charges. Petrol vehicles need Euro 4 (2006+) for ULEZ compliance.

blocks.question: Does a diesel save money on fuel- +
blocks.answer: Yes - diesel is typically 12-16p per mile vs 16-20p for petrol. At 15,000 miles/year, diesel saves £500-£1,000/year in fuel. But this saving can be eroded by higher repair costs, ULEZ charges, and declining resale value. Calculate your total cost of ownership, not just fuel cost.

blocks.question: What's the resale value of diesel vs petrol- +
blocks.answer: Petrol resale value is stable . Diesel resale value is declining , especially for pre-Euro 6 diesels, due to ULEZ/CAZ restrictions and changing buyer preferences. High-mileage diesels are particularly difficult to sell.

blocks.question: Can I still buy a diesel car in 2026- +
blocks.answer: Yes - but only if it's Euro 6 compliant and you drive enough miles (15k+) to justify the higher costs. For urban drivers, petrol is almost always the better choice. New diesel car sales are declining, but used diesels remain widely available.

blocks.question: What's the best fuel type for short trips- +
blocks.answer: Petrol is strongly recommended for short trips. Diesel engines need long motorway journeys for DPF regeneration; short trips cause DPF clogging and expensive repairs. Petrol engines have simpler emissions systems and are more reliable for urban driving.
